entrypoints.summary: An authenticated user submits title and content through POST /write; content is stored in that user's note array.
An authenticated user can add a numbered note to share_notes via GET /share_diary/:id and can request a bot visit through GET /report with numeric id and username query parameters.
The shared-note page consumes id and username from the URL fragment and fetches the selected shared note.

affected_components.role: Persists notes, exposes shared notes selected by username, and dispatches bot visits.
Fetches shared note data and assigns content to innerHTML.
Creates the bot session, installs the FLAG cookie, and navigates to the shared-note fragment URL.

impact.affected_asset: The bot's script-readable FLAG cookie, whose value is read from /flag.txt.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause browser-side script execution in the report bot's localhost shared-note origin by placing executable HTML in a shared note and having the bot load that note.
impact.security_effect: Potential disclosure of the FLAG cookie available to the report bot's shared-note page.

causal_trace.summary: Authenticated note creation accepts attacker-controlled content shorter than 256 characters and persists it in the notes map.

A selected attacker note can be appended to the creator's share_notes list, and the shared-note API returns its content for a supplied username and numeric index without requiring a session when username is provided.
The shared-note client obtains the note JSON and assigns data.content to a paragraph element's innerHTML, interpreting stored content as HTML rather than displaying it as text.

The report route invokes a Puppeteer visitor for the supplied id and username; that visitor sets a non-HttpOnly FLAG cookie for localhost before loading the shared-note URL. Thus markup script execution in that bot page can access the challenge secret cookie in the page origin.

failure.operation: Assignment of returned shared-note content to content.innerHTML

primary_invariant.statement: Persisted diary content returned by the shared-note API must be rendered as inert text and must not create executable markup in the shared-note viewer's origin.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The client directly assigns the returned content field to innerHTML after fetching the selected shared note.

quality.review_notes: The supplied primary source establishes the storage, sharing, innerHTML sink, bot navigation, and non-HttpOnly cookie setup. No exploit payload, browser execution result, cookie-exfiltration trace, response-template/CSP evidence, or remediation patch is present. The repository is an archive mirror rather than demonstrated organizer-origin provenance.

remediation.invariant_restored: Render returned diary content as text (or otherwise ensure it cannot be interpreted as active markup), and keep the secret unavailable to page script through a non-HttpOnly cookie.
mitigation_classes: inert text rendering of untrusted note content
avoid placing secrets in script-readable cookies

target.component: shared diary-note viewer and report bot
